text:
Mira (PM): Quick sync — proposing we compress launch scope to a 3-feature minimum so we can hit an internal canary on Apr 8 and a public launch target of Apr 22. Need engineering + sales input on customer blockers.

Mira (PM): Proposed MVP minset:
- Authoring core (editor + promptstore)
- Serving via Redwood API (hosted endpoint, streaming)
- Embeddings + vector search for retrieval

Mira (PM): Defer to v1: SSO/SAML, advanced billing workflows, admin settings page, and multi-tenant RBAC.

Dmitri (Eng Lead): From eng perspective this is doable if we drop SSO and the admin settings. Main risk is embedding infra load — we need to limit shard parallelism for the canary.

Dmitri (Eng Lead): Also need to flag autoscaling: without the prepared autoscaler rules we'll have to cap concurrency per customer to protect latency SLOs.

Kevin (Design): We can trim the settings UI. For MVP we deliver a minimal onboarding flow + inline help. UX can remove the advanced account management screens.

Matt (Infra): Autoscaler readiness is currently at ~60%. If we want full public traffic by Apr 22 we need 2 more weeks of testing OR we keep Apr 8 canary internal-only with a hard traffic cap.

Sam (Sales): FYI Acme and NovaCorp have SAML required for pilots. They told me they could accept an early access canary if we guarantee SSO in v1 within 6 weeks. Need written commitment.

Anya (CS): We have two customers (FinEdge, RetailCo) flexible on SSO; they prefer early access to validate quality. So a limited canary could work.

Mira (PM): Proposed launch gates (must all pass for public launch):
```
- Gate 1: Internal canary for 72h with <1% error rate
- Gate 2: Latency p95 < 600ms on canary traffic profile
- Gate 3: Autoscaler plays well under ramp (no manual intervention > 4h)
- Gate 4: Sign-off from CS for pilot invite list
```

Mira (PM): If any gate fails, public launch moves to Apr 22 and we keep an Apr 8 internal canary. Decision needed today: do we accept limited canary + SSO in v1 (6 weeks) or hold everything for SSO?

Dmitri (Eng Lead): I can accept limited canary + commit to SSO in v1 if product owners accept constrained concurrency and feature-flagged rollout. I'll add the approach to the PRD.

Sam (Sales): Sales OK with that tradeoff provided we send signed emails committing to v1 SSO ETA. We'll need a short customer-facing note explaining canary limits and timeline.

Anya (CS): I'll draft the pilot invite + FAQ and get it out to FinEdge and RetailCo tomorrow.

Kevin (Design): I'll scope the reduced onboarding and provide mocks by EOD.

Matt (Infra): I'll prepare autoscaler guardrails and a traffic cap config — putting a temporary cap of 50 rps per org for the canary.

Mira (PM): Decision summary:
- MVP (canary Apr 8 internal, limited pilot invites) = Authoring + API + Embeddings
- Defer SSO, admin settings to v1 (target: 6 weeks after canary)
- Public launch gated on the 4 gates; if any fail public launch -> Apr 22
- Eng: implement concurrency cap + feature flags; Infra: autoscaler guardrails
- CS/Sales: communicate pilot constraints to customers

Mira (PM): Next steps: Dmitri to update the PRD and rollout playbook; Matt to publish cap config; Anya to send pilot invite draft; Kevin to drop mocks.

release-bot: deploy pipeline queued for branch `mvp-minset` — preview env available at https://preview.redwood.local/abc123

Anya (CS): noted, will ping when invite is ready. :white_check_mark: 

Dmitri (Eng Lead): I'll post a short follow-up with the thread of engineering risks and a proposed rollback plan within 2 hours.

Mira (PM): Thanks everyone — this is the scope path I'll take into stakeholder update unless anyone objects in the next hour. :+1:
